subject: Dedicated capacity discovery — Valora recap & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@valora.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery — recap & next steps

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and I can pull together a proposal that maps to Valora’s constraints. I’ve bolded the asks where I need artifacts from your side.

Key pain points you shared:
- Production latency spikes during batch reconciliation windows (95th percentile jumps to ~700ms).
- Unpredictable token costs on current managed endpoints during high-volume jobs.
- Data isolation requirement for transaction-level PII (PCI-adjacent workflows).

Current stack / constraints:
- Model: internally fine-tuned llama-2 style model served via an in-house microservice (gRPC) that currently calls hosted endpoints for embedding + generation.
- Peak batch traffic: 1200 requests/min for batched inference (5–10s context windows). Typical steady-state TPS: 4–6 TPS.
- Region: primarily us-west2.
- Procurement window: Q4 approval preferred; target go-live by mid-Nov.

Success criteria you highlighted:
1) 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for single-request gen workloads (after warmup).
2) Predictable monthly unit cost below your current blended price by at least 25% for inference volume.
3) Logical/physical isolation for models and logs (must meet your internal audit team baseline).

Dedicated capacity fit notes (preliminary):
- Reserved GPU pool: your workload suggests starting with a 4-GPU reserved pool (A100- or H100-class); recommend an initial pilot with 4 reserved GPUs + burst to 8 for peak windows.
- Autoscaling/burst policy: suggestion to enable scheduled burst windows (cron-based) tied to reconciliation jobs and an on-demand burst for manual spikes.
- Isolation: we can provide VPC-only private deployment with customer-managed KMS for keys; can also ship a Private deployment package if required for audit.

Action items / asks (next steps):
1) Please share a ~24-hour trace of your inference requests (anonymized) or a sample payload set so we can run a throughput/latency simulation (**valora_inference_sample.json** would work).
2) Confirm any hard latency targets besides the 95th <= 350ms line above.
3) Procurement POC & estimated budget range (so I can size pilot vs reserved commit).
4) Any compliance docs your security/infosec team requires upfront (SOC2 evidence, encryption requirements).

Timeline proposal from our side:
- Week 0: exchange sample traces + security checklist.
- Week 1–2: Redwood runs bench runs and proposes pilot config + expected costs.
- Week 3–6: 6-week pilot (reserved pool w/ burst) + success evaluation.

Attachments: I’ve attached a brief checklist and a one‑page pilot proposal for internal reading.

If that matches your expectations I’ll get a draft pilot SOW and schedule the bench-run for early next week.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Thanks Ben — this is perfect and aligns with what I captured. A few clarifications: 

- I attached the sample payloads and a short anonymized traffic trace (see valora_inference_sample.json). Those are representative of both batch and single-request flows.
- Our budget band for a pilot is $40k–$60k over the engagement (including any reserved capacity + benching work).
- Procurement timeline: we need a statement of work by Oct 20 to hit our internal Q4 approval cycle.
- Compliance: security will need KMS controls + an audit trail for key rotations; SOC2 evidence would be helpful but we can start with the checklist.

We also have a hard constraint on model isolation for any environment that stores transaction metadata — that rules out shared-tenant storage of logs.

Happy to have Procurement coordinate with you directly (procurement@valora.ai) for contract/legal steps.

Elena
Elena Martinez
Head of Platform, Valora AI
